flagged.title: The Peasants' Revolt, 1381
flagged.reason: The video presents the storming of the Tower and beheading of Sudbury as occurring on June 13 before the Mile End meeting on June 14, and repeats the outdated figure of 150 executions instead of at least 1,500.

mark_affecting.quote: June 13th, Wat Tyler's men cross London Bridge ... Step 3 ... they actually storm the Tower of London itself ... The mob dragged out Archbishop Simon Sudbury ... along with Robert Hales, the Treasurer ... dragged out, beheaded
Roughly 150 of the rebel ringleaders were hunted down and executed.

flagged.title: The English Revolution: Civil War, Regicide and Republic, 1642-1660
flagged.reason: The video repeats the debunked claim that Rainsborough's specific language directly inspired the Chartists, teaching a false historical fact about the transmission of the Putney Debates (which were lost until 1890).

mark_affecting.quote: that specific language is going to echo through history, inspiring reformers like the Chartists, and the suffragettes centuries later.
